metaTitle: Jaguar V8 Supercharged Timing Chain Repair (AJ133/AJ126) | Jaguar Garage
metaDescription: Jaguar V8 timing chain repair for AJ133 and AJ126 engines at Jaguar Garage. Specialist timing chain replacement for 5.0 V8 and 3.0 V6 supercharged engines.
h1: Jaguar V8 Supercharged Timing Chain Repair
lede: Specialist timing chain replacement for Jaguar AJ133 5.0 V8 and AJ126 3.0 V6 supercharged engines – carried out in our Essex workshop.

blocks.html: Timing chain replacement on the Jaguar AJ133 5.0 V8 and AJ126 3.0 V6 supercharged engines involves accessing the front of the engine, removing the timing cover, and replacing the timing chains, tensioners, guide rails, and associated components. The AJ133 and AJ126 use the same timing chain system, with only a minor difference in the auxiliary chain drive – the 5.0 version uses a tensioner guide and guide rail, while the 3.0 version uses only the tensioner guide with a balance weight sprocket in place of the guide rail.[reference:0]

There are two distinct timing component designs across these engines: an early Tsubaki system with 6.35mm pitch chains, and a later INA system with 8mm pitch chains.[reference:1] The INA system, which is more common, features a steel tensioner plunger that contacts an aluminium guide rail – the updated design incorporates a steel insert in the guide rail for the tensioner to push against.[reference:2] Our technicians are trained on both systems and replace components with the correct updated parts for your engine.

Work on the timing chains can be carried out with the engine in situ – the engine does not need to be removed for this procedure.[reference:3][reference:4] However, if additional work such as head gasket replacement is required, engine removal may be necessary.[reference:5]

steps.title: Access & Preparation
steps.body: We remove ancillary components – air intake, drive belts, and the harmonic balancer. The crankshaft is immobilised using a holding tool to allow removal of the balancer.[reference:6] The front timing cover is then removed to expose the timing chain drive.

steps.title: Component Removal
steps.body: We release tension on the timing chains, then remove the camshaft and crankshaft sprockets.[reference:7] The existing chains, tensioners, and guide rails are removed and inspected.

steps.title: Chain & Component Replacement
steps.body: New timing chains, tensioners, and guide rails are installed. We use updated OEM components – for the INA system, this includes guide rails with steel inserts for the tensioner to push against.[reference:8][reference:9] The correct chain type (Tsubaki or INA) is fitted based on the engine's original specification.

steps.title: Timing Alignment
steps.body: Using specialist timing tools – camshaft alignment tools (OEM 303-1445), crankshaft timing pin (OEM 303-1447), flywheel locking tool (OEM 303-1448), and timing chain pre-tensioning tool (OEM 303-1482) – we set the camshaft and crankshaft to the correct positions.[reference:10] The upper timing chain tensioner bolt is torqued to approximately 55 Nm to ensure proper chain preload and timing accuracy.[reference:11]

steps.title: Reassembly & Testing
steps.body: The timing cover is refitted with new seals, and all ancillary components are reinstalled. The engine is then started and run to operating temperature, and a full road test is carried out to confirm correct timing, performance, and absence of chain noise.

items.q: What does a timing chain replacement on a Jaguar V8 involve?
items.a: We access the front of the engine, remove the timing cover, and replace the timing chains, tensioners, and guide rails. The work is carried out using specialist timing tools to ensure correct camshaft and crankshaft alignment. The engine can remain in the vehicle for this procedure.

items.q: What is the difference between the Tsubaki and INA timing systems?
items.a: The early Tsubaki system uses 6.35mm pitch chains, while the later INA system uses 8mm pitch chains.[reference:15] The INA system features a steel tensioner plunger that contacts an aluminium guide rail – updated guide rails with steel inserts are available to address this design.[reference:16]

items.q: Does the engine need to be removed for timing chain replacement?
items.a: No – work on the timing chains can be carried out with the engine in situ.[reference:17][reference:18] However, if additional work such as head gasket replacement is required, engine removal may be necessary.[reference:19]

items.q: What specialist tools do you use for this repair?
items.a: We use the Baum Tools BJAG303-1445KIT timing kit, which includes camshaft alignment tools, a crankshaft timing pin, a flywheel locking tool, a camshaft turning tool, and a timing chain pre-tensioning tool.[reference:20][reference:21]

items.q: Do I need to book an inspection?
items.a: We recommend an initial inspection so we can assess the condition of your timing chain system. You can [request a quote](/contact) to start the process.
